# Purpose

This is the **odds-ratio companion** to the GBSG analysis in `quarto/gbsg/analysis_gbsg_mr.qmd`, and the first
analysis in this workstream on the package's **GLM path**: a binary outcome, an odds ratio in place of a hazard
ratio, and the thresholds supplied on the OR scale.

One forest-search fit selects the subgroup under the max N(ε) criterion, and multiplier resampling (MR), computed
inside the same fit, gives the selection-adjusted bounds the operating-characteristics simulations evaluate:

- the **field** one-sided lower bound on $\beta(\hat H)$, the effect in the identified region;
- the **field-s** one-sided upper bound on $\beta(\hat H^c)$, the effect in its complement;
- the **Bonferroni pair** joining them, for a claim about both subgroups at once.

Beside them are the **unadjusted** analysis, which treats the region as fixed in advance, and the **two-term de-biased
estimate**, which is the centre of every bound. Its two-sided IJ interval is carried as a reference only. Quantities that exist only in
simulation are not reported.

Nothing here is resampled by refitting. No full bootstrap, cross-validation, DINA or GRF analysis is run.

::: {.callout-important}
## The outcome is on the adverse scale: OR above 1 is harm

The analysed outcome is **`y_binary_neg`, the indicator of *no* CD4 improvement** — the complement of the
CD4-improvement indicator, deliberately flipped so that the search runs in the same direction as on the survival
path. An odds ratio **above** 1 therefore means the treatment raises the odds of **no improvement**, which is
**harm**; an odds ratio below 1 means fewer non-improvers, which is benefit.

Read every number below on that scale. A reader who assumes the CD4-improvement scale will read every sign
backwards.
:::

| Setting | Value | Source |
|---|---|---|
| `sg_focus` | `effMaxSG` | the max N(ε) criterion |
| `effect_neighborhood` | **0.20** | this workstream's ε, as GBSG and panitumumab (the published ACTG175 analysis used 0.10) |
| `selection_rule` | `neighborhood` | the current template; `max_subgroups_search` is left at the package default, `Inf` |
| outcome | `y_binary_neg`, no CD4 improvement at week 20 (adverse scale) | the template |
| `outcome_type` / `effect_measure` | **`binary` / `OR`** | the template; `OR` must be set, since the binary default is `RD` |
| `adverse_outcome` | `TRUE` | the template |
| c1, screening threshold (`effect.threshold`) | **1.00** | the template. On the GLM path the thresholds arrive through `effect.threshold` / `consistency.threshold`, which overwrite `hr.threshold` / `hr.consistency` |
| c2, per-split threshold (`consistency.threshold`) | **1.00** | the same |
| p\*, consistency proportion (`pconsistency.threshold`) | **0.90** | the same |
| `consistency_method` | `resample` | set explicitly; the GLM MR path requires it |
| covariates | age, prior antiretroviral therapy, weight, Karnofsky score, baseline CD4 and CD8, and six binary indicators | the template |
| cuts | J = 10 on baseline CD4 and weight; default cuts elsewhere | the template |
| MR | `ci_method = "field"`, 5,000 multiplier draws, complement and field-s on, two-term IJ residual | the simulations' settings |
| field Monte Carlo | 1,000 outer × 500 inner draws | package defaults, not settable through `forestsearch()` |
| nominal level | one-sided 0.95; Bonferroni pair joint 0.95 (0.975 per side) | fixed in the package |

## Subgroup descriptions

Subgroup definitions are carried in the payloads in the search's own coding. In this document's
tables and prose they are rendered in plain language. A negated comparison is flipped, so `cd40 <= 380` negated reads
"baseline CD4 count > 380 per mm³". A negated flag takes the covariate's complement label, so not-male reads
"female". The map below is the whole translation, and every label is taken from the `speff2trial::ACTG175`
documentation: `race` is 0 white and 1 non-white; `gender` is 0 female and 1 male; `homo` is homosexual activity;
`drugs` is a history of intravenous drug use; `symptom` is the symptomatic indicator; `karnof` is the Karnofsky
score on a 0–100 scale; `preanti` is the number of days of previously received antiretroviral therapy; `cd40` and
`cd80` are the baseline CD4 and CD8 T cell counts, in the per-cubic-millimetre units the trial's eligibility range
is quoted in.

```{r label-map}
covariate_labels <- data.frame(
  covariate  = c("age", "preanti", "wtkg", "karnof", "cd40", "cd80",
                 "hemo", "homo", "drugs", "race", "gender", "symptom"),
  label      = c("age", "prior antiretroviral therapy", "weight", "Karnofsky score",
                 "baseline CD4 count", "baseline CD8 count",
                 "hemophilia", "homosexual activity", "history of intravenous drug use",
                 "non-white", "male", "symptomatic"),
  unit       = c("years", "days", "kg", "", "per mm³", "per mm³", "", "", "", "", "", ""),
  complement = c(NA, NA, NA, NA, NA, NA,
                 "no hemophilia", "no homosexual activity", "no history of intravenous drug use",
                 "white", "female", "asymptomatic"),
  stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
knitr::kable(transform(covariate_labels, unit = ifelse(nzchar(unit), unit, "—"),
                       complement = ifelse(is.na(complement), "—", complement)),
             col.names = c("Covariate", "Label", "Unit", "Complement label"), row.names = FALSE,
             caption = "Covariate label map (the translation table itself), from the speff2trial::ACTG175 documentation.")

.parse_term <- function(term) {
  term <- trimws(term)
  neg  <- startsWith(term, "!")
  body <- sub("^!?\\{(.*)\\}$", "\\1", term)
  m <- regmatches(body, regexec("^([A-Za-z0-9_.]+)\\s*(<=|>=|<|>|==)\\s*(\\S+)$", body))[[1]]
  if (length(m) == 4L) list(var = m[2], op = m[3], value = as.numeric(m[4]), neg = neg)
  else list(var = body, op = NA_character_, value = NA_real_, neg = neg)
}
.flip <- c("<=" = ">", ">=" = "<", "<" = ">=", ">" = "<=")
.sym  <- c("<=" = "≤", ">=" = "≥", "<" = "<", ">" = ">", "==" = "=")
describe_subgroup <- function(def) {
  terms <- strsplit(def, " & ", fixed = TRUE)[[1]]
  out <- vapply(terms, function(tm) {
    p <- .parse_term(tm); i <- match(p$var, covariate_labels$covariate)
    if (is.na(i)) stop("no label for covariate ", p$var)
    if (is.na(p$op)) {
      if (!p$neg) return(covariate_labels$label[i])
      if (is.na(covariate_labels$complement[i])) stop("no complement label for ", p$var)
      return(covariate_labels$complement[i])
    }
    op <- if (p$neg) .flip[[p$op]] else p$op
    trimws(sprintf("%s %s %s %s", covariate_labels$label[i], .sym[[op]], format(p$value), covariate_labels$unit[i]))
  }, character(1))
  paste(out, collapse = " and ")
}
# the same rule, evaluated: membership of each subject in the described subgroup
subgroup_member <- function(def, d) {
  terms <- strsplit(def, " & ", fixed = TRUE)[[1]]
  Reduce(`&`, lapply(terms, function(tm) {
    p <- .parse_term(tm); x <- d[[p$var]]; stopifnot(!is.null(x))
    v <- if (is.na(p$op)) x == 1 else switch(p$op, "<=" = x <= p$value, ">=" = x >= p$value,
                                               "<" = x < p$value, ">" = x > p$value, "==" = x == p$value)
    if (p$neg) !v else v
  }))
}
# Gate 4: a description carries no coding characters and no column name, and denotes the payload's set (by N)
raw_names <- c("preanti", "wtkg", "karnof", "cd40", "cd80", "cd420", "hemo", "homo", "drugs",
               "race", "gender", "symptom", "arms", "y_binary_pos", "y_binary_neg")
check_description <- function(def, N, d) {
  s <- describe_subgroup(def)
  bad <- grepl("[{}!]", s) || any(vapply(raw_names, function(k) grepl(paste0("\\b", k, "\\b"), s), TRUE))
  if (bad) stop("description still carries coding: ", s)
  if (sum(subgroup_member(def, d)) != N) stop("description of ", def, " does not give N = ", N)
  s
}
```

# Data

`speff2trial::ACTG175` holds all four arms of the trial. This analysis uses the two the post-selection manuscript
uses: **arm 1, zidovudine + didanosine, as the treatment, against arm 3, didanosine alone, as the control**. The
preparation below is the template's, written out in full.

```{r setup}
suppressPackageStartupMessages({
  library(forestsearch)
  library(speff2trial)
})
t_doc <- proc.time()[["elapsed"]]

df <- subset(speff2trial::ACTG175, arms %in% c(1L, 3L))
n_arms13 <- nrow(df)
df$id    <- seq_len(nrow(df))
df$treat <- ifelse(df$arms == 1L, 1L, 0L)         # 1 = ZDV + ddI, 0 = ddI

# Drop subjects with no week-20 CD4 measurement
n_dropped <- sum(is.na(df$cd420))
df <- df[!is.na(df$cd420), ]

# The beneficial scale, then the adverse scale the search runs on
df$y_binary_pos <- as.integer(df$cd420 > df$cd40)   # 1 = CD4 improved
df$y_binary_neg <- 1L - df$y_binary_pos             # 1 = no CD4 improvement (the analysed outcome)

# every candidate covariate numeric: forestsearch builds "var <= value" cuts, and cont.cutoff = 4
# treats the 0/1 indicators as categorical automatically
bin_vars  <- c("hemo", "homo", "drugs", "race", "gender", "symptom")
cont_vars <- c("age", "preanti", "wtkg", "karnof", "cd40", "cd80")
for (v in bin_vars) df[[v]] <- as.numeric(df[[v]])
confounders <- c(cont_vars, bin_vars)

stopifnot(n_arms13 == 1083, n_dropped == 0, nrow(df) == 1083,
          !anyNA(df[c(confounders, "y_binary_neg", "treat")]),
          identical(df$y_binary_neg, 1L - df$y_binary_pos),
          all(df$y_binary_neg %in% 0:1), setequal(unique(df$arms), c(1L, 3L)),
          all(vapply(bin_vars, function(v) setequal(unique(df[[v]]), 0:1), TRUE)))
c(subjects = nrow(df), ZDV_ddI = sum(df$treat == 1), ddI = sum(df$treat == 0),
  no_improvement = sum(df$y_binary_neg), improved = sum(df$y_binary_pos),
  dropped_missing_week20_CD4 = n_dropped)
```

## Reference effects

Each bound below is read against the whole-trial effect and against the marginal strata of the covariates that define
the selected subgroup, never against OR 1.00 alone.

```{r reference-effects}
# Unadjusted odds ratio of the adverse outcome, treatment against control, with a Wald interval.
# A cell is fitted only where each arm has at least min_per_arm adverse outcomes and at least
# min_per_arm non-adverse ones; otherwise the logistic fit is separated or unstable.
or_est <- function(d, min_per_arm = 0, y = "y_binary_neg") {
  ev <- tapply(d[[y]], factor(d$treat, levels = 0:1), sum)
  n  <- tapply(d[[y]], factor(d$treat, levels = 0:1), length)
  ev[is.na(ev)] <- 0L; n[is.na(n)] <- 0L
  non <- n - ev
  out <- data.frame(n = nrow(d), n_ctrl = n[["0"]], n_trt = n[["1"]],
                    ev_ctrl = ev[["0"]], ev_trt = ev[["1"]],
                    or = NA_real_, lo = NA_real_, hi = NA_real_)
  if (min(ev, non) < max(1, min_per_arm)) return(out)
  f  <- glm(d[[y]] ~ d$treat, family = binomial)
  b  <- coef(f)[[2]]; se <- sqrt(diag(vcov(f)))[[2]]
  out$or <- exp(b); out$lo <- exp(b - qnorm(0.975) * se); out$hi <- exp(b + qnorm(0.975) * se)
  out
}
fci <- function(e, l, u, d = 3) ifelse(is.na(e), "—", sprintf("%.*f (%.*f, %.*f)", d, e, d, l, d, u))

ref_sets <- list(
  "whole trial"               = rep(TRUE, nrow(df)),
  "weight > 86 kg"            = df$wtkg > 86,
  "weight ≤ 86 kg"            = df$wtkg <= 86,
  "baseline CD4 > 380 per mm³" = df$cd40 > 380,
  "baseline CD4 ≤ 380 per mm³" = df$cd40 <= 380)
reference_or <- do.call(rbind, lapply(names(ref_sets), function(k)
  cbind(set = k, or_est(df[ref_sets[[k]], ]))))
rownames(reference_or) <- NULL
knitr::kable(data.frame(set = reference_or$set, N = reference_or$n,
                        `ZDV+ddI / ddI` = sprintf("%d / %d", reference_or$n_trt, reference_or$n_ctrl),
                        `no improvement (ZDV+ddI / ddI)` = sprintf("%d / %d", reference_or$ev_trt, reference_or$ev_ctrl),
                        `OR (95% CI)` = fci(reference_or$or, reference_or$lo, reference_or$hi),
                        check.names = FALSE),
             row.names = FALSE,
             caption = "Odds ratio of NO CD4 improvement, ZDV + ddI against ddI (logistic, Wald 95%). OR above 1 is harm.")
```

# The fit

One call. Identification, the unadjusted estimates and every MR quantity come out of it together. The GLM-path
arguments — `outcome_type`, `effect_measure`, `adverse_outcome`, and the thresholds through `effect.threshold` and
`consistency.threshold` — are named as the installed `forestsearch()` signature names them. On the binary path the
outcome is its own event, so `event.name` is the outcome column.

```{r fit}
mr_draws <- 5000L
t0 <- proc.time()[["elapsed"]]
fit <- forestsearch(
  df.analysis = df,
  outcome.name = "y_binary_neg", event.name = "y_binary_neg", treat.name = "treat", id.name = "id",
  confounders.name = confounders,
  is.RCT = TRUE, seedit = 8316951,
  outcome_type = "binary", effect_measure = "OR", adverse_outcome = TRUE,
  use_lasso = FALSE, use_grf = FALSE, use_dina = FALSE,
  max_n_confounders = 1000,
  cut_type = "default", cont.cutoff = 4, conf.cont_jcuts = list(cd40 = 10, wtkg = 10),
  collapse_cuts = TRUE,
  subgroup_method = "consistency", sg_focus = "effMaxSG",
  selection_rule = "neighborhood", effect_neighborhood = 0.20,
  n.min = 60, d0.min = 10, d1.min = 10, maxk = 2, max_subgroups_search = Inf,
  effect.threshold = 1.00, consistency.threshold = 1.00, pconsistency.threshold = 0.90,
  consistency_method = "resample", m1.threshold = Inf, minp = 0.025, fs.splits = 1000,
  stop_threshold = NULL,
  mr_inference = TRUE,
  mr_inference_args = list(ci_method = "field", draws = mr_draws, include_complement = TRUE,
                           confirm_rule = "point", field_uniform = FALSE,
                           field_complement = TRUE, ij_residual = "two_term",
                           field_decompose = TRUE, field_scale_complement = "selected",
                           field_recovery = FALSE, return_reselection = TRUE,
                           keep_declaration_field = TRUE, keep_field_matrix = FALSE,
                           declaration_c0 = c(0.70, 0.75, 0.80, 0.85)))
fit_sec <- proc.time()[["elapsed"]] - t0
if (fit_sec > 900) stop(sprintf("the fit took %.0f s, over the 15-minute cap", fit_sec))
g <- fit$mr_inference
cat(sprintf("forestsearch %s; fit including MR: %.1f s (multiplier stage %.1f s; field blocks %.1f + %.1f s)\n",
            packageVersion("forestsearch"), fit_sec, g$timing_seconds,
            g$field$timing_seconds, g$field$complement$timing_seconds))
```

## The settings the package received, and that MR ran

Read back from the fit's own record of its arguments, not from the call above.

```{r settings-received}
keys <- c("outcome_type", "effect_measure", "adverse_outcome", "effect.threshold", "consistency.threshold",
          "hr.threshold", "hr.consistency", "pconsistency.threshold", "consistency_method",
          "sg_focus", "selection_rule", "effect_neighborhood", "max_subgroups_search", "n.min", "maxk")
received <- fit$args_call_all[keys]
knitr::kable(data.frame(argument = keys,
                        received = vapply(received, function(x) paste(format(x), collapse = ", "), "")),
             row.names = FALSE, caption = "fit$args_call_all, as recorded by forestsearch().")
stopifnot(identical(received$outcome_type, "binary"), identical(received$effect_measure, "OR"),
          isTRUE(received$adverse_outcome), identical(received$consistency_method, "resample"),
          received$effect.threshold == 1, received$consistency.threshold == 1,
          received$hr.threshold == 1, received$hr.consistency == 1,          # the aliases overwrite these
          received$pconsistency.threshold == 0.9,
          # the package records sg_focus under its canonical name: "effMaxSG" resolves to "hrMaxSG"
          received$sg_focus %in% c("effMaxSG", "hrMaxSG"),
          identical(received$selection_rule, "neighborhood"), received$effect_neighborhood == 0.20,
          is.infinite(received$max_subgroups_search))

# Gate: MR ran. Checked on the returned object, not on the absence of an error.
stopifnot(!is.null(g), is.list(g$field), is.list(g$field$complement), is.list(g$field$joint_s),
          !is.na(fit$mr_harm_confirmed), is.finite(g$naive$est), is.finite(g$debiased$est),
          is.finite(g$field$lower_1s), is.finite(g$field$complement$upper_1s_s),
          identical(g$measure, "OR"), g$n_family > 0)
cat(sprintf("MR ran: measure %s, log scale %s, family %d, harm confirmed %s (rule: %s).\n",
            g$measure, g$log_scale, g$n_family, fit$mr_harm_confirmed, g$settings$confirm_rule))
```

## The selection, and the candidate funnel

There is **no committed ACTG175 criteria payload**, so unlike GBSG there is no stored row to reproduce. The
selection this fit produces is the reference for later work.

```{r selection}
label_fs <- paste(fit$sg.harm, collapse = " & ")
est <- fit$df.est
in_H <- est$treat.recommend[match(df$id, est$id)] == 0
stopifnot(!anyNA(in_H), identical(in_H, subgroup_member(label_fs, df)))
n_H <- sum(in_H); n_Hc <- sum(!in_H)
or_H <- or_est(df[in_H, ])$or
fcn <- fit$find.grps$filter_counts
funnel <- data.frame(
  stage = c("candidates enumerated", "fittable", "clearing the OR screen (≥ 1.00)",
            "evaluated for consistency", "passing consistency (p* = 0.90)", "MR candidate family"),
  n = c(fcn$n_evaluated, fcn$n_passed_cox, fcn$n_passed_hr,
        fit$grp.consistency$n_candidates_evaluated, fit$grp.consistency$n_passed, g$n_family))
knitr::kable(funnel, col.names = c("", "count"), row.names = FALSE, caption = "The candidate funnel.")

# the consistency-passing candidates. On the GLM path this table's `hr` column is the log odds ratio.
cand <- as.data.frame(fit$grp.consistency$out_sg$result)
mcols <- grep("^M\\.", names(cand), value = TRUE)
cand_def <- apply(cand[, mcols, drop = FALSE], 1, function(z) paste(z[nzchar(z) & !is.na(z)], collapse = " & "))
cand_tab <- data.frame(
  subgroup = vapply(seq_along(cand_def), function(i) check_description(cand_def[i], cand$N[i], df), ""),
  N = cand$N, `no improvement` = cand$E, OR = sprintf("%.3f", exp(cand$hr)), Pcons = sprintf("%.2f", cand$Pcons),
  check.names = FALSE)
knitr::kable(cand_tab, row.names = FALSE,
             caption = "Candidates passing the consistency screen, ordered as the package returns them; the first row is the max N(ε) selection. The package's own table carries the effect as a log odds ratio on this path; it is exponentiated here.")
stopifnot(abs(exp(cand$hr[1]) - or_H) < 1e-8, cand$N[1] == n_H, identical(unname(cand_def[1]), label_fs))
```

# The Pareto frontier

The figure below is drawn by the package's own `forestsearch::plot_pareto_frontier()`, from this document's fit,
unwrapped and unmodified. It reads `fs$grp.consistency$out_sg$pareto_frontier`, so it needs no payload and no second
fit.

**It is not the analogue of the GBSG and panitumumab frontier figures.** Those are drawn by the manuscript's
`criteria_fig()` from a criteria payload, and mark **six selection criteria's choices** on one shared candidate
frontier. This one shows **a single fit's frontier, with that fit's own selection highlighted**. No criteria payload
exists for ACTG175, and none is created here.

Two things to read with the figure. **The effect axis is the natural odds ratio**: the function exponentiates the
frontier's stored log-OR for a ratio measure and labels the axis "Odds ratio". **The member labels carry the search's
raw column names** (`cd40`, `wtkg`), because the package has no covariate lookup — the same divergence the GBSG and
panitumumab figures have from their documents' tables, which use the label map above. The axis limits are set through
the function's own `xlim` argument, because its default trim clips two of those labels at the frame; nothing else is
changed, and the package is not modified.

```{r frontier-figure, fig.width = 6.5, fig.height = 4.2}
frontier <- fit$grp.consistency$out_sg$pareto_frontier
stopifnot(data.table::is.data.table(frontier), nrow(frontier) > 0L)

p_frontier <- forestsearch::plot_pareto_frontier(
  fit,
  show_band = TRUE,                  # fires here: fit$sg_focus is the canonical "hrMaxSG"
  effect_neighborhood = 0.20,        # the band this analysis selects within
  label_members = TRUE,
  point_size = 3,
  # the default trim (5% padding on a ratio measure) clips the leftmost and the selected member's
  # label at the frame; widening through the function's own xlim argument clears both
  xlim = c(1.45, 4.35))
stopifnot(inherits(p_frontier, "ggplot"))

# the highlighted point is this analysis's selection, checked on the plotted data
pd  <- p_frontier$data
sel <- pd[which(pd$is_selected), ]
stopifnot(nrow(sel) == 1L, sel$N == n_H, identical(sel$label, label_fs),
          abs(sel$hr - or_H) < 1e-8, sum(pd$is_selected) == 1L)

ggplot2::ggsave("fig_actg175_pareto_frontier.png", p_frontier,
                width = 6.5, height = 4.2, dpi = 200, bg = "white")
cat(sprintf("Frontier members: %d of the %d candidates passing consistency; selected %s (N %d, OR %.3f).\n",
            nrow(frontier), fit$grp.consistency$n_passed, describe_subgroup(sel$label), sel$N, sel$hr))
p_frontier
```

The frontier holds `r nrow(frontier)` of the `r fit$grp.consistency$n_passed` candidates that pass consistency: the
fifth is dominated on both axes and so is not a frontier member. The shaded band is the ε = 0.20 neighbourhood of the
maximum effect, within which max N(ε) takes the largest subgroup; here the maximum is also the only member inside it.

# The data set

`speff2trial::ACTG175` is complete on every covariate this analysis uses, and no subject in the two arms is missing
the week-20 CD4 count, so the analysis set is the whole two-arm subset.

```{r cascade}
cascade <- data.frame(
  population = c("Trial, four arms", "Arms 1 and 3", "Analysis set", "Selected / complement"),
  N = c(format(nrow(speff2trial::ACTG175)), format(n_arms13), format(nrow(df)),
        sprintf("%d / %d", n_H, n_Hc)),
  what_it_is = c(
    "every subject in the package's data set; the other two arms are not analysed",
    "arm 1 (ZDV + ddI) and arm 3 (ddI), the two arms the post-selection manuscript compares",
    sprintf("arms 1 and 3 less %d with no week-20 CD4 count; %d ZDV + ddI, %d ddI; %d with no CD4 improvement",
            n_dropped, sum(df$treat == 1), sum(df$treat == 0), sum(df$y_binary_neg)),
    "the max N(ε) split"))
knitr::kable(cascade, col.names = c("Population", "N", "What it is"), align = "lrl", row.names = FALSE,
             caption = "The counts.")
```

# Selection-adjusted bounds

```{r extract}
cc <- g$complement
fb <- g$field
fc <- fb$complement
js <- fb$joint_s

bounds <- list(
  field_lower_H     = fb$lower_1s,
  field_s_upper_Hc  = fc$upper_1s_s,
  bonf_lower_H      = js$bonf_lower_H,
  bonf_upper_Hc     = js$bonf_upper_Hc,
  bonf_joint_prob   = js$bonf_joint_prob,
  calib_gamma       = js$gamma,
  calib_joint_prob  = js$joint_prob,
  calib_lower_H     = js$lower_H,
  calib_upper_Hc    = js$upper_Hc,
  joint_corr        = js$corr,
  n_joint_draws     = js$n_joint_draws,
  rho_c             = fc$decomp_fields$scale_ratio_c,
  n_out_H           = fb$n_out_used,
  n_in_H            = fb$n_in_used_mean,
  n_out_Hc          = fc$n_out_used,
  field_sec_H       = fb$timing_seconds,
  field_sec_Hc      = fc$timing_seconds,
  alpha             = js$alpha,
  # the field's second-order point estimates: est2 = exp(two-term log-OR - lambda_mean), lambda_mean the mean of
  # the simulated root on the log scale (fs_mr_inference(): field$est2, field$lambda_mean; the complement block
  # carries the same pair for the unstudentized root and, with the _s suffix, for field-s, the reported product)
  field_est2_H            = fb$est2,
  field_lambda_mean_H     = fb$lambda_mean,
  field_s_est2_Hc         = fc$est2_s,
  field_s_lambda_mean_Hc  = fc$lambda_mean_s,
  field_est2_Hc           = fc$est2,
  field_lambda_mean_Hc    = fc$lambda_mean)
stopifnot(is.finite(bounds$field_est2_H), is.finite(bounds$field_lambda_mean_H),
          is.finite(bounds$field_s_est2_Hc), is.finite(bounds$field_s_lambda_mean_Hc),
          abs(bounds$field_est2_H - exp(log(g$debiased$est) - bounds$field_lambda_mean_H)) < 1e-10,
          abs(bounds$field_s_est2_Hc - exp(log(cc$debiased$est) - bounds$field_s_lambda_mean_Hc)) < 1e-10)

ev_H  <- sum(df$y_binary_neg[in_H]); ev_Hc <- sum(df$y_binary_neg[!in_H])
stopifnot(ev_H + ev_Hc == sum(df$y_binary_neg))   # the two regions' adverse outcomes make up the analysis set's
h3 <- function(x) sprintf("%.3f", x)
ci <- function(l, u) sprintf("%s–%s", h3(l), h3(u))
whole <- reference_or[1, ]
summary_table <- data.frame(
  row = c("**Reference effects**", "Whole trial",
          "**Identified subgroup**", "Unadjusted", "Two-term", "Field, lower bound",
          "**Complement**", "Unadjusted", "Two-term", "Field-s, upper bound"),
  N = c("", whole$n, "", n_H, n_H, n_H, "", n_Hc, n_Hc, n_Hc),
  Events = c("", whole$ev_ctrl + whole$ev_trt, "", ev_H, "—", "—", "", ev_Hc, "—", "—"),
  OR = c("", h3(whole$or), "",
         h3(g$naive$est), h3(g$debiased$est), h3(bounds$field_est2_H), "",
         h3(cc$naive$est), h3(cc$debiased$est), h3(bounds$field_s_est2_Hc)),
  CI = c("", ci(whole$lo, whole$hi), "",
         ci(g$naive$lower, g$naive$upper), paste(ci(g$debiased$lower, g$debiased$upper), "†"),
         paste(h3(bounds$field_lower_H), "‡"), "",
         ci(cc$naive$lower, cc$naive$upper), paste(ci(cc$debiased$lower, cc$debiased$upper), "†"),
         paste(h3(bounds$field_s_upper_Hc), "‡")),
  stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
knitr::kable(summary_table,
             col.names = c("", "N", "No CD4 improvement", "OR", "95% CI"), align = "lrrrl", row.names = FALSE,
             caption = sprintf("Odds ratios of NO CD4 improvement, ZDV + ddI against ddI; OR above 1 is harm. Whole trial: %d on ZDV + ddI, %d on ddI. Identified subgroup: %s.",
                               whole$n_trt, whole$n_ctrl, check_description(label_fs, n_H, df)))
```

† Two-sided infinitesimal-jackknife interval, reference only.

‡ One-sided 95%, inverted around the two-term estimate. Bonferroni pair, joint 95%:
`r h3(bounds$bonf_lower_H)` and `r h3(bounds$bonf_upper_Hc)`.

```{r est2-reading, echo = FALSE}
ord_H <- bounds$field_lower_H <= bounds$field_est2_H && bounds$field_est2_H <= g$debiased$est
first_H <- log(g$naive$est) - log(g$debiased$est)
first_Hc <- log(cc$naive$est) - log(cc$debiased$est)
```

**The field rows.** Their OR is the field's second-order estimate, `est2`: the two-term estimate less the mean of the
simulated root, $\bar\Lambda$, on the log scale. The one-sided bound in the same row is **not** centred on it. The bound is
inverted around the two-term estimate, subtracting a quantile of the same simulated law where `est2` subtracts its mean.

- **The identified subgroup.** $\bar\Lambda$ = `r sprintf("%.4f", bounds$field_lambda_mean_H)` on the log-OR scale, against a
  first correction (unadjusted to two-term) of `r sprintf("%.4f", first_H)`. `est2` is `r h3(bounds$field_est2_H)`,
  against the two-term `r h3(g$debiased$est)`. The ordering bound ≤ `est2` ≤ two-term
  `r if (ord_H) "holds" else "**does not hold**"`
  (`r h3(bounds$field_lower_H)`, `r h3(bounds$field_est2_H)`, `r h3(g$debiased$est)`)`r if (bounds$field_lambda_mean_H <= 0) ": the mean of the simulated root is not positive, so est2 sits at or above the two-term estimate" else ""`.
- **The complement (field-s).** $\bar\Lambda$ = `r sprintf("%.4f", bounds$field_s_lambda_mean_Hc)`, against a first correction of
  `r sprintf("%.4f", first_Hc)`. `est2` is `r h3(bounds$field_s_est2_Hc)`, against the two-term `r h3(cc$debiased$est)`.

```{r diagnostics}
diag_tab <- data.frame(
  quantity = c("candidate family (MR)", "selection bias, log-OR (harm side)",
               "selection bias, log-OR (complement)",
               "field outer / mean inner draws used (harm)", "field outer draws used (complement)",
               "Bonferroni pair: simulated joint coverage",
               "calibrated split: gamma, simulated joint coverage",
               "calibrated split: lower (H-hat), upper (complement)",
               "correlation of the aligned roots",
               "scale ratio rho-c (selected complement / re-selections)",
               "wall time (s): fit + MR; MR multiplier stage; harm field; complement field"),
  value = c(format(g$n_family), sprintf("%.4f", g$selection_bias), sprintf("%.4f", cc$selection_bias),
            sprintf("%d / %.0f", bounds$n_out_H, bounds$n_in_H), format(bounds$n_out_Hc),
            sprintf("%.4f", bounds$bonf_joint_prob),
            sprintf("%.3f, %.4f", bounds$calib_gamma, bounds$calib_joint_prob),
            sprintf("%.3f, %.3f", bounds$calib_lower_H, bounds$calib_upper_Hc),
            sprintf("%.3f", bounds$joint_corr), sprintf("%.3f", bounds$rho_c),
            sprintf("%.1f; %.1f; %.1f; %.1f", fit_sec, g$timing_seconds,
                    bounds$field_sec_H, bounds$field_sec_Hc)))
knitr::kable(diag_tab, row.names = FALSE, caption = "Supporting quantities. The calibrated split checks the Bonferroni pair; it is not a second product.")
```

## Each bound against the trial's effect sizes

```{r location}
thr <- c(0.50, 0.67, 0.80, 1.00, 1.25, 1.50, 2.00)
loc <- data.frame(
  bound = c("field lower, H-hat", "Bonferroni lower, H-hat",
            "field-s upper, complement", "Bonferroni upper, complement"),
  value = c(bounds$field_lower_H, bounds$bonf_lower_H, bounds$field_s_upper_Hc, bounds$bonf_upper_Hc),
  side  = c("lower", "lower", "upper", "upper"))
loc$excludes <- ifelse(loc$side == "lower",
  sprintf("OR below %.3f", loc$value), sprintf("OR above %.3f", loc$value))
loc$thresholds_cleared <- vapply(seq_len(nrow(loc)), function(i) {
  hit <- if (loc$side[i] == "lower") thr[loc$value[i] >= thr] else thr[loc$value[i] <= thr]
  if (length(hit)) paste(sprintf("%.2f", hit), collapse = ", ") else "none"
}, character(1))
loc$whole_trial <- sprintf("%.3f", reference_or$or[1])
knitr::kable(loc[, c("bound", "value", "excludes", "thresholds_cleared", "whole_trial")],
             digits = 3, row.names = FALSE,
             caption = "On the adverse scale. A lower bound clears a threshold at or below it; an upper bound clears one at or above it. Thresholds 0.50, 0.67, 0.80, 1.00, 1.25, 1.50, 2.00.")
```

# Declaration calibration {#sec-declcal}

**Pre-specification.** Stated before any number below was read.

- **The claim.** Harm is claimed at c1 = 1.00 (the screen) and c2 = 1.00 (the per-split consistency threshold) on the
  odds-ratio scale of the **adverse** outcome, no CD4 improvement, harm = OR > 1, exactly as the rest of this document
  uses them: unchanged.
- **The protected level c0.** The clinically meaningful uniform benefit against which the false-declaration rate is
  controlled: c0 ∈ {0.70, 0.75, 0.80, 0.85} on the same OR scale, where benefit is OR < 1 (fewer patients without
  CD4 improvement), **primary 0.75**. The grid on the odds-ratio scale is carried over from the hazard-ratio grid used
  in the survival application rather than derived from a clinical margin for CD4 response; this document states no
  such margin. It is pre-specified in the sense that it is fixed before the calibration is read, and it may be
  replaced by a margin chosen on clinical grounds. These are pre-specified constants, never the observed whole-trial
  effect. All satisfy c0 ≤ c2.
- **α = 0.10**, family-wise, over the pre-reduction candidate family.

**What is computed.** The screen that chose $\hat H$ admits a candidate $g$ when
$T(g) = (\hat\beta(g) - \log c_2)/\sigma_D(g) \ge$ `r sprintf("%.3f", fs_declaration_calibration(fit, alpha = 0.10)$z_pstar)`, the cutoff the package applies at p\* = 0.90; that is the
closed-form consistency rule, relabelled. Under the shared-multiplier law of the fit's own MR draws, the maximum of
$T$ over the candidate family, with every candidate shifted to sit at c0, has a 0.90 quantile $\hat\kappa_{0.10}$(c0).
The calibrated rule admits $g$ when $T(g) \ge \hat\kappa_{0.10}$(c0), which holds the family-wise probability of
declaring any harm subgroup at 0.10 whenever every candidate's true effect is c0 or better. The field is read from
the 5,000 draws the fit above already made (`keep_declaration_field = TRUE`, with the grid passed as
`declaration_c0`); nothing is redrawn, and the fit's other outputs are unchanged by it. The capture fired, so the
field comes from the fit itself. The calibrated rule is applied on $T(g)$ directly: `forestsearch()` is **not**
re-run: the calibrated rule is applied to $T(g)$ directly, and the settable pair is guidance on what p\* to set.

```{r declcal}
c0_grid <- c(0.70, 0.75, 0.80, 0.85); c0_primary <- 0.75
c1_nat <- 1.00; c2_nat <- 1.00; fmt_c0 <- function(x) sprintf("%.2f", x)   # the claim, natural scale
stopifnot(!is.null(g$declaration_field), identical(g$declaration_field$meta$c0, c0_grid))   # the capture fired
cal    <- fs_declaration_calibration(fit, alpha = 0.10, c0 = c0_grid)
cal_c2 <- fs_declaration_calibration(fit, alpha = 0.10)                  # c0 = NULL: the c2 boundary
cal_05 <- fs_declaration_calibration(fit, alpha = 0.05, c0 = c0_grid)    # stored in the payload, not reported
stopifnot(identical(cal$c0$source, "capture"), cal$n_family_prereduction == g$n_family,
          isTRUE(cal$reduction$replay_check), !is.null(cal$screened),
          length(cal$screened) == fit$grp.consistency$n_candidates_evaluated)
z_scr <- cal$z_pstar   # the p* = 0.90 screen's cutoff as the package applies it (its print's "T >= ...")
stopifnot(length(z_scr) == 1L, is.finite(z_scr), identical(z_scr, cal_c2$z_pstar))
cal
```

```{r declcal-table}
# The family's identifiers are the search's factor codes: q<i>.1 is the i-th evaluated factor, q<i>.0 its negation.
fam_def <- function(id) vapply(strsplit(id, " & ", fixed = TRUE), function(p) {
  i <- as.integer(sub("^q(\\d+)\\.[01]$", "\\1", p))
  paste0(ifelse(endsWith(p, ".0"), "!", ""), "{", fit$confounders.evaluated[i], "}", collapse = " & ")
}, "")
fld  <- g$declaration_field
id_H <- fld$family_id[fld$meta$selected_index]
stopifnot(identical(fam_def(id_H), label_fs))
T_by_candidate <- data.frame(id = names(cal$T_hat), definition = fam_def(names(cal$T_hat)),
                             N = unname(fld$meta$sizes[names(cal$T_hat)]),
                             beta_hat = unname(cal$beta_hat), sigma_D = unname(cal$sigma_D),
                             T = unname(cal$T_hat), screened = names(cal$T_hat) %in% cal$screened)
i_max <- which.max(T_by_candidate$T)
max_T <- as.list(T_by_candidate[i_max, c("id", "definition", "N", "T", "screened")])
T_H   <- cal$T_hat[[id_H]]

# The applied admitted set: the calibrated set over the pre-reduction family, intersected with the
# candidates this document's own screen evaluated. Intersecting can only remove declarations.
adm     <- c(cal$c0$admitted_calibrated, list(c2 = cal_c2$admitted_calibrated))
applied <- lapply(adm, intersect, cal$screened)
tb      <- cal$c0$table
kappa   <- c(tb$kappa_hat, cal_c2$kappa_hat)
# The settable-pair columns, all of them, under the package's names and in its order, for the c0 rows. The c2 row
# comes from the c0 = NULL call, which returns none of them, so its cells are left blank.
st_nm <- c("pstar_settable", "pstar_achievable", "pcons_eff_settable", "z_eff_settable", "z_gap",
           "digits_fine", "pstar_fine", "z_gap_fine")
stopifnot(identical(names(tb)[names(tb) %in% st_nm], st_nm))
st     <- tb[st_nm]
st_fmt <- data.frame(
  pstar_settable     = formatC(st$pstar_settable, format = "f", digits = cal$digits),
  pstar_achievable   = as.character(st$pstar_achievable),
  pcons_eff_settable = formatC(st$pcons_eff_settable, format = "f", digits = cal$digits + 1L),
  z_eff_settable     = sprintf("%.3f", st$z_eff_settable),
  z_gap              = sprintf("%.3f", st$z_gap),
  digits_fine        = sprintf("%d", st$digits_fine),
  pstar_fine         = vapply(seq_len(nrow(st)), function(i) if (is.na(st$digits_fine[i])) "NA" else
                                formatC(st$pstar_fine[i], format = "f", digits = st$digits_fine[i]), ""),
  z_gap_fine         = sprintf("%.4f", st$z_gap_fine))
st_fmt <- rbind(st_fmt, as.data.frame(as.list(setNames(rep("", length(st_nm)), st_nm))))
stopifnot(identical(names(st_fmt), st_nm))
declcal_table <- data.frame(
  c0       = c(paste0(fmt_c0(tb$c0), ifelse(tb$c0 == c0_primary, " (primary)", "")),
               paste0(fmt_c0(c2_nat), ", the c2 boundary (c0 = c2)")),
  kappa    = sprintf("%.3f", kappa),
  st_fmt,
  fw       = sprintf("%.3f", c(tb$fw_size, cal_c2$fw_size)),
  admitted = sprintf("%d (%d)", lengths(applied), lengths(adm)),
  H_cal    = vapply(applied, function(a) if (length(a)) paste(describe_subgroup(fam_def(a)), collapse = "; ")
                    else "none", ""))
knitr::kable(declcal_table, row.names = FALSE, align = paste0("lr", strrep("r", length(st_nm)), "rrl"),
             col.names = c("c0 (OR)", "κ̂₀.₁₀", paste0("`", st_nm, "`"), "FŴ₀.₁₀ of the p\\* = 0.90 screen at c0",
                           "candidates the calibrated rule admits", "calibrated Ĥ"),
             caption = sprintf("Declaration calibration at α = 0.10. Admitted, k (m): k in the applied set, the calibrated admitted set intersected with the %d candidates this document's screen evaluated; m in the calibrated admitted set over the pre-reduction family of %d.",
                               length(cal$screened), cal$n_family_prereduction))
```

*The settable-pair columns, in the package's words (`?fs_declaration_calibration`), at the fit's
`pconsistency.digits` = `r cal$digits`: `pstar_settable`, the smallest p\* on the 10^−digits grid whose effective
threshold is at or above κ̂(c0); that threshold as `pcons_eff_settable` (Pcons scale) and `z_eff_settable` (z scale);
`z_gap` = `z_eff_settable` − κ̂(c0) (positive = conservative); and `digits_fine` / `pstar_fine` / `z_gap_fine`, the
smallest digits (searched over 1 to 12) at which the gap falls below 0.01, with its p\*. When no p\* ≤ 1 reaches
κ̂(c0) at the fit's digits, `pstar_achievable` is FALSE and the settable columns are NA. This is guidance on what to
set, not an identity: the settable screen is κ̂(c0) rounded up to what the grid can express, so it admits a subset of
what κ̂(c0) admits. The package reports the settable pair for the c₀ rows only.*

*FŴ at c0 is the family-wise probability that the p\* = 0.90 screen declares a harm subgroup if every candidate's
true effect were a uniform benefit of c0 — a property of this trial's candidate family and covariate design, not
an estimate of the trial's realized error rate.*

**The observed statistic.** The maximum of $T$ ranges over the pre-reduction family of
`r format(cal$n_family_prereduction, big.mark = ",")` candidates: every enumerated candidate of at most two factors
meeting the size minimum, before the near-duplicate reduction.

```{r declcal-observed}
obs_tab <- data.frame(c0 = declcal_table$c0, kappa = declcal_table$kappa,
                      gap_max = sprintf("%.3f", kappa - max_T$T), gap_H = sprintf("%.3f", kappa - T_H))
knitr::kable(obs_tab, row.names = FALSE, align = "lrrr",
             col.names = c("c0 (OR)", "κ̂₀.₁₀", "κ̂ − max T", "κ̂ − T(Ĥ)"),
             caption = sprintf("Maximum over the family: T = %.3f, %s (N %d)%s. The declared subgroup, %s (N %d): T = %.3f. The p* = 0.90 screen's cutoff is %.3f.",
                               max_T$T, check_description(max_T$definition, max_T$N, df), max_T$N,
                               if (max_T$screened) ", among the candidates the screen evaluated" else ", a candidate the screen did not evaluate",
                               describe_subgroup(label_fs), n_H, T_H, z_scr))
```

**The calibrated Ĥ.**

```{r declcal-decision}
# The readings below are written for an empty applied set at every c0; the document stops otherwise.
if (any(lengths(applied) > 0)) stop("the calibrated rule admits a candidate: the calibrated-H section must be rewritten")
stopifnot(max_T$T < min(kappa), identical(max_T$id, names(which.max(cal$T_hat[cal$screened]))))
i_p <- which(tb$c0 == c0_primary)
```

The applied admitted set is empty at every c0 on the grid, and at the c2 boundary. **No subgroup is declared harmful
at {c1, c2} = {`r fmt_c0(c1_nat)`, `r fmt_c0(c2_nat)`} with 10% family-wise protection against a uniform benefit of
OR 0.75 or better.** At no c0 on the grid would the observed maximum clear: its closest approach is
`r sprintf("%.3f", min(tb$kappa_hat) - max_T$T)` below $\hat\kappa_{0.10}$ at c0 = `r fmt_c0(tb$c0[which.min(tb$kappa_hat)])`.
The pre-reduction maximum sits on a candidate the screen evaluated, so the intersection removes nothing here. With
no calibrated Ĥ, there are no bounds to set beside the document's.

## Interpretation {#sec-declcal-interpretation}

```{r declcal-interp, echo = FALSE}
fw_p <- tb$fw_size[i_p]; kap_p <- tb$kappa_hat[i_p]
```

- **What FŴ says about the p\* = 0.90 screen.** If every one of these `r format(cal$n_family_prereduction, big.mark = ",")`
  candidates carried a uniform benefit of OR 0.75, the screen as run would declare some harm subgroup in
  `r round(100 * fw_p)`% of perturbation draws; with every candidate at the c2 boundary, in
  `r round(100 * cal_c2$fw_size)`%. That is the size of this family and this covariate design, not the trial's
  realized error rate.
- **What the screen's cutoff would have to be.** Holding the family-wise rate at 0.10 against OR 0.75
  needs $T(g) \ge$ `r sprintf("%.2f", kap_p)`, against the screen's `r sprintf("%.3f", z_scr)`: a settable p\* of
  `r if (isTRUE(tb$pstar_achievable[i_p])) sprintf("%s (z_gap %.3f)", formatC(tb$pstar_settable[i_p], format = "f", digits = cal$digits), tb$z_gap[i_p]) else sprintf("none at pconsistency.digits = %d (pstar_achievable FALSE, z_gap NA)", cal$digits)` in place of 0.90.
- **Where the observed maximum sits.** It is `r sprintf("%.2f", max_T$T)`, below $\hat\kappa_{0.10}$ at every c0 on the
  grid (`r sprintf("%.2f", min(tb$kappa_hat))` to `r sprintf("%.2f", max(tb$kappa_hat))`) and at the c2 boundary
  (`r sprintf("%.2f", cal_c2$kappa_hat)`). `r if (identical(max_T$id, id_H)) "It is attained by the declared subgroup itself." else paste0("It is attained by ", describe_subgroup(max_T$definition), ", not by the declared subgroup.")`
- **The declared subgroup.** Its own $T$ is `r sprintf("%.2f", T_H)`: it clears the screen's `r sprintf("%.3f", z_scr)`, which is why it
  was declared, and falls `r sprintf("%.2f", kap_p - T_H)` short of the calibrated cutoff at the primary c0.
- **The calibrated decision at the primary c0.** No subgroup is declared harmful: the p\* = 0.90 screen's declaration of Ĥ does not carry 10% family-wise
  protection against OR 0.75.
- **What is unchanged.** The selection, and every bound and estimate reported above, are those of the fit as run;
  the calibration reads that fit and alters none of them.

# Classification agreement

The post-selection manuscript's ACTG175 table reports three regions on these data, from three identifiers. The
max N(ε) selection here is set against the **published descriptions** of the other two, over all `r nrow(df)`
subjects. Those descriptions are read from the manuscript's table caption; the fits behind them are not re-run
here, and DINA and GRF are not run at all.

```{r agreement}
def_grf  <- "!{wtkg <= 84.3696} & !{cd40 <= 368.2}"    # GRF, as the published caption gives the cuts
def_dina <- "{preanti >= 849.4} & {cd40 >= 338}"       # DINA
in_grf  <- df$wtkg > 84.3696 & df$cd40 > 368.2
in_dina <- df$preanti >= 849.4 & df$cd40 >= 338
stopifnot(identical(in_grf, subgroup_member(def_grf, df)), identical(in_dina, subgroup_member(def_dina, df)))
published_n <- c(fs = 72L, grf = 95L, dina = 98L)
agreement_note <- c(
  sprintf("published FS n %d; this fit n %d", published_n[["fs"]], n_H),
  sprintf("published GRF n %d; the caption's cuts give %d here", published_n[["grf"]], sum(in_grf)),
  sprintf("published DINA n %d; the caption's cuts give %d here", published_n[["dina"]], sum(in_dina)))

agree2x2 <- function(A, B, nameA, nameB) {
  cells <- list(both = A & B, A_only = A & !B, B_only = !A & B, neither = !A & !B)
  names(cells) <- c("in both", paste0("in ", nameA, " only"), paste0("in ", nameB, " only"), "in neither")
  stopifnot(sum(vapply(cells, sum, 0)) == length(A))
  po <- mean(A == B); pa <- mean(A); pb <- mean(B)
  pe <- pa * pb + (1 - pa) * (1 - pb)
  tab <- do.call(rbind, lapply(names(cells), function(k)
    cbind(cell = k, or_est(df[cells[[k]], ], min_per_arm = 10))))
  list(table = tab,
       n_total = length(A), n_A = sum(A), n_B = sum(B),
       proportion_agreeing = po,
       kappa = if (pe < 1) (po - pe) / (1 - pe) else NA_real_,
       jaccard = sum(A & B) / sum(A | B))
}
show_agree <- function(x, caption) {
  t <- x$table
  print(knitr::kable(data.frame(cell = t$cell, N = t$n, `ZDV+ddI / ddI` = sprintf("%d / %d", t$n_trt, t$n_ctrl),
                                `no improvement (ZDV+ddI / ddI)` = sprintf("%d / %d", t$ev_trt, t$ev_ctrl),
                                `OR (95% CI)` = fci(t$or, t$lo, t$hi), check.names = FALSE),
                     row.names = FALSE, caption = caption))
  cat(sprintf("\nCells sum to %d of %d. Proportion agreeing %.3f; Cohen's kappa %.3f; Jaccard index on the selected side %.3f (%d of %d in the union).\n\n",
              sum(t$n), x$n_total, x$proportion_agreeing, x$kappa, x$jaccard,
              t$n[1], t$n[1] + t$n[2] + t$n[3]))
}

agreement <- list(
  maxNeps_vs_grf  = agree2x2(in_H, in_grf,  "max N(ε)", "published GRF region"),
  maxNeps_vs_dina = agree2x2(in_H, in_dina, "max N(ε)", "published DINA region"),
  definitions = c(max_N_eps = label_fs, published_grf = def_grf, published_dina = def_dina),
  published_n = published_n, notes = agreement_note,
  min_per_arm_for_or = 10L)
```

```{r agreement-tables, results = "asis"}
show_agree(agreement$maxNeps_vs_grf, sprintf("Max N(ε) against the published GRF region, %s. Cells fitted where each arm has at least 10 in both outcome categories.", check_description(def_grf, sum(in_grf), df)))
show_agree(agreement$maxNeps_vs_dina, sprintf("Max N(ε) against the published DINA region, %s. Cells fitted where each arm has at least 10 in both outcome categories.", check_description(def_dina, sum(in_dina), df)))
```

# Payload

The payload follows the same shape as the GBSG and panitumumab payloads, so a supplement section can read them the
same way. Nothing refit-based was run, so the FB columns and `meta$B` are `NA`. The estimate scale is the odds
ratio, recorded in `est_scale`.

```{r payload}
harm_rates <- local({
  h <- df[in_H, ]
  et <- h$y_binary_neg[h$treat == 1]; ec <- h$y_binary_neg[h$treat == 0]
  list(treated_n = length(et), control_n = length(ec),
       treated_events = sum(et == 1), control_events = sum(ec == 1),
       treated_pct = 100 * mean(et == 1), control_pct = 100 * mean(ec == 1))
})
table1 <- data.frame(
  method = "FS", region = c("H", "Hc"),
  n = c(n_H, n_Hc), pct = round(100 * c(n_H, n_Hc) / nrow(df)),
  naive_est = c(g$naive$est, cc$naive$est), naive_lo = c(g$naive$lower, cc$naive$lower),
  naive_hi = c(g$naive$upper, cc$naive$upper),
  fb_est = NA_real_, fb_lo = NA_real_, fb_hi = NA_real_,
  mr_est = c(g$debiased$est, cc$debiased$est), mr_lo = c(g$debiased$lower, cc$debiased$lower),
  mr_hi = c(g$debiased$upper, cc$debiased$upper),
  stringsAsFactors = FALSE)

si <- sessionInfo()
```

# Interpretation {#sec-interpretation}

```{r interp-values, echo = FALSE}
r2 <- function(x) sprintf("%.2f", x)
r3 <- function(x) sprintf("%.3f", x)
ref <- setNames(reference_or$or, reference_or$set)
cleared <- setNames(loc$thresholds_cleared, loc$bound)
cells <- function(x) setNames(split(x$table, seq_len(nrow(x$table))), c("both", "A", "B", "neither"))
gr <- agreement$maxNeps_vs_grf;  gr_t <- cells(gr)
dn <- agreement$maxNeps_vs_dina; dn_t <- cells(dn)
# the readings below are written for these locations; the document stops if a bound lands elsewhere
stopifnot(bounds$field_lower_H < 1, bounds$field_s_upper_Hc < 1, bounds$bonf_upper_Hc < 1,
          bounds$bonf_lower_H < 1, g$naive$est > 2, g$debiased$est > 1,
          ref[["whole trial"]] < 1,
          # the readings name where each bound sits relative to the whole-trial effect
          bounds$field_lower_H > ref[["whole trial"]], bounds$bonf_lower_H < ref[["whole trial"]],
          bounds$field_s_upper_Hc > ref[["whole trial"]])
```

Every statement below is read from the bound's location, on the adverse scale, where an odds ratio **above** 1 means
more patients with no CD4 improvement under treatment. None is a test at an odds ratio of 1.00, which is where the
screen that chose the subgroup was set. The whole trial's odds ratio is `r r3(ref[["whole trial"]])`: on these two
arms, the combination therapy leaves **fewer** patients without CD4 improvement.

**The selected subgroup.**

- **What was selected.** Max N(ε) returned `r describe_subgroup(label_fs)`: `r n_H` of `r nrow(df)` patients
  (`r round(100 * n_H / nrow(df))`%), `r harm_rates$treated_n` on ZDV + ddI and `r harm_rates$control_n` on ddI. In
  it, `r sprintf("%.1f", harm_rates$treated_pct)`% of the treated show no CD4 improvement against
  `r sprintf("%.1f", harm_rates$control_pct)`% of the controls.
- **Unadjusted.** Its odds ratio is `r r2(g$naive$est)` (`r r2(g$naive$lower)`, `r r2(g$naive$upper)`): on its face,
  a large effect in the harm direction, and the reverse of the whole trial's.
- **The correction.** It removes a selection bias of `r r2(g$selection_bias)` on the log-OR scale, over a family of
  `r g$n_family` candidates, and the two-term estimate is `r r2(g$debiased$est)`.
- **The field lower bound is `r r2(bounds$field_lower_H)`.** The data exclude only odds ratios below
  `r r2(bounds$field_lower_H)` — that is, only a benefit larger than that. The bound clears
  `r cleared[["field lower, H-hat"]]` of the thresholds 0.50–2.00, and does not reach 1.00.
- **Reading.** **Harm in this subgroup is not established.** After correction the data are consistent with harm, with
  no effect, and with benefit down to an odds ratio of `r r2(bounds$field_lower_H)`. That bound sits just **above** the
  whole-trial `r r3(ref[["whole trial"]])`, so a benefit of the whole trial's size is only marginally excluded here —
  by `r sprintf("%.3f", bounds$field_lower_H - ref[["whole trial"]])` on the odds-ratio scale. The unadjusted
  `r r2(g$naive$est)` is largely what the selection produced.

**The complement.**

- **Unadjusted and corrected.** `r n_Hc` patients: unadjusted OR `r r2(cc$naive$est)`, corrected `r r2(cc$debiased$est)`.
- **The field-s upper bound is `r r2(bounds$field_s_upper_Hc)`.** The data exclude odds ratios above
  `r r2(bounds$field_s_upper_Hc)`, so outside the selected subgroup a reduction of at least
  `r round(100 * (1 - bounds$field_s_upper_Hc))`% in the odds of no CD4 improvement is established. The bound clears
  `r cleared[["field-s upper, complement"]]`.
- **Against the trial.** The whole-trial `r r3(ref[["whole trial"]])` is within what the bound allows.
- **Why field-s adds little here.** The scale ratio is `r r3(bounds$rho_c)`, so field-s and the unstudentized field
  nearly agree.

**The two-subgroup claim.**

- **The pair.** The Bonferroni pair is `r r2(bounds$bonf_lower_H)` for the selected subgroup and
  `r r2(bounds$bonf_upper_Hc)` for its complement, each at one-sided 0.975.
- **Why it is not conservative here.** Its simulated joint coverage is `r r3(bounds$bonf_joint_prob)`. The calibrated
  split settles at γ = `r r3(bounds$calib_gamma)`, Bonferroni's own α/2, and the aligned roots correlate at
  `r r2(bounds$joint_corr)`.
- **What the claim amounts to.**
  - **The complement.** Its benefit, a reduction of at least `r round(100 * (1 - bounds$bonf_upper_Hc))`% in the odds
    of no improvement, survives the joint adjustment.
  - **The selected subgroup.** It excludes only odds ratios below `r r2(bounds$bonf_lower_H)`, which is no claim of harm.
  - **So** a claim that the two subgroups differ is not supported. The claim of benefit outside the subgroup is.

**Against the published regions.**

- **GRF.** The published GRF region, `r describe_subgroup(def_grf)`, shares `r gr_t$both$n` patients with max N(ε)
  (Jaccard `r r2(gr$jaccard)`, κ `r r2(gr$kappa)`). They are near-duplicates of one another: the cuts differ slightly
  and the membership differs for `r gr_t$A$n + gr_t$B$n` patients.
- **DINA.** The published DINA region, `r describe_subgroup(def_dina)`, is a different set:
  `r dn_t$both$n` shared, Jaccard `r r2(dn$jaccard)`.
- **What is not done here.** Neither identifier is re-run, and no correction is recomputed for them. These are
  membership comparisons against published descriptions only.

**What this analysis does not establish.**

- **Coverage.** The bounds' coverage is established by simulation, including a binary design built on these
  covariates. These data are that design's source, so this analysis is not an independent check of it.
- **The thresholds.** c1 = c2 = 1.00 on the OR scale, and p\* = 0.90, are the template's and this workstream's
  settings, not a clinical calibration.
- **The candidate family.** MR's family is every size-eligible candidate. It is a superset of the one the search chose
  among, and the package notes that this inflates the selection-bias term.
- **The subset.** Only arms 1 and 3 are analysed, as in the post-selection manuscript. Nothing here speaks to the
  trial's other two arms.
- **What was not run.** No full bootstrap was run.
